notes: Read the full unit, foreign-policy context, all fourteen candidates and the review. Identified the U.S. institutions, resolved Citizens United as the U.S. Supreme Court decision, split the two electoral mechanisms while preserving their all-elections scope, and restored both the working-class-governance rationale for systemic change and the anti-corruption measures' stated relation to ending legalized bribery.

claims.claim_text: Ending U.S. political corruption and legalized bribery would include eliminating lobbyists and dark money and overturning the U.S. Supreme Court's Citizens United decision.
Working-class government is said to require a new U.S. political system.
Replace the U.S. president and Supreme Court with an executive and judiciary selected by and subordinate to Congress.
Replace the U.S. two-party system with a multiparty democracy.
Expand the U.S. House of Representatives.
Implement proportional representation in all U.S. elections.
Implement ranked-choice voting in all U.S. elections.
